# IOG script flags

The flag registry names and documents the script flags (the bit array `$0A00`-`$0AB3`) of the Illusion of Gaia (US) baserom. It is **hand-curated through one tool**, `npm run flags`, and everything below the line "Registry overview (generated)" is generated from it by `npm run flags -- docs`. Plan: `plans/flags/flag-analysis-plan.md`.

## How to read this page set

- A flag is addressed by its **global index** `n` (decimal in the files, `$hex` in text): WRAM byte `$0A00 + (n >> 3)`, bit `n & 7`, mask `1 << (n & 7)`. Index 63 = `$003F` = byte `$0A07`, mask `$80`. COP byte and word operands address the same array.
- The index space is split into **domains** D1-D9 (table below). `$0000`-`$000F` (D1) are **scene scratch**: zeroed at every scene load, so the same index means different things in different scenes and every D1 record carries a scene scope. Everything else is persistent (save block) except D6, which is reset on world-map entry.
- One index can have several **meanings**, each with a `scope` (`null` = everywhere, or a list of scenes). A persistent index has either one global meaning or, when the index is reused, only scoped meanings.
- A **name** states what is true when the flag is set (`ec_lance_letter_shown`). A **grade** says how sure we are: `VERIFIED-RUNTIME` (A/B trial in Mesen2), `VERIFIED-STATIC` (every reader and writer read, effect unambiguous), `INFERRED` (consistent with context), `UNKNOWN` (sites known, meaning not established).
- Pages: one page per area (a group of `db-us/groups.json`, or `system`), linked from the Areas table. Generated pages carry the sites (ROM offset, file:line, opcode, role) when `plans/flags/inventory.json` exists.

## Files

| File | Written by | Content |
|------|-----------|---------|
| `db-us/flags.json` | `npm run flags -- <fragment>` | The registry: `domains`, `flags` (per index: meanings), `proposals` |
| `db-us/scene-flags.json` | `npm run flags -- scene-flags <spec>` | Per scene: the flags the player needs on arrival (`flags`, `names`, `entry`, `grade`, `note`, `source`); read by `export scenes` |
| `db-us/flag-presets.json` | `npm run flags -- presets <spec>` | Named story checkpoints (flags, items, form, abilities) |
| `artifacts/flags.json`, `artifacts/flag-presets.json` | `npm run flags -- export` | Flat machine exports for the Mesen2 Lua kit and the Python harness |
| `docs/flags/*.md` | `npm run flags -- docs` | This page set (`_intro.md` is the only hand-written file) |
| `plans/flags/inventory.json`, `inventory.md` | `npm run flags -- inventory` (FL01) | Static site inventory of the line-tracked `extracted/` tree; its `sites` are joined into the export and the docs |

Never edit these by hand and never write a script that does: the tool validates everything and writes the canonical form (sorted indices, fixed field order, 2-space indent, CRLF kept). `--check` reports a file that is not in that form.

## Commands

```
npm run flags -- <fragment.json> [--dry-run]            merge flag records into db-us/flags.json
npm run flags -- --check [--strict]                     validate the three db-us files against each other
npm run flags -- export [--out-dir=<dir>]               artifacts/flags.json + artifacts/flag-presets.json
npm run flags -- docs [--out-dir=<dir>]                 docs/flags/README.md + one page per area
npm run flags -- scene-flags <spec.json> [--dry-run]    merge entries into db-us/scene-flags.json
npm run flags -- presets <spec.json> [--dry-run]        merge into db-us/flag-presets.json
npm run flags -- inventory [--dry-run]                  scan extracted/ into plans/flags/inventory.json + inventory.md
npm run flags -- inventory --compare=<old.json> [--compare-out=<file>]   also reconcile with an older inventory
```

Options: `--db-dir=<dir>` (every command; default `db-us`; point it at a copy to try something), `--inventory=<file>` (`export`, `docs`; default `plans/flags/inventory.json`), `--out=<file>`, `--md=<file>`, `--extracted=<dir>` (`inventory` only; defaults `plans/flags/inventory.json`, `plans/flags/inventory.md`, `extracted`). Without `--dry-run` a merge writes; with it nothing is written, ever.

Conventions are those of `merge` and `names`: a spec file goes in, everything is validated before any write, **one rejected record aborts the whole run** (nothing written; every rejection is listed with its reason and the counts show `xN rejected`), a file is rewritten only when its content changed, and re-applying a spec reports `=unchanged`. Exit code is non-zero on any error, so it can gate a script. `--check` exits non-zero on errors; with `--strict` warnings fail too (the apply pass uses `--check --strict`).

### Typical session

```
npm run flags -- plans/flags/results/registry/FL21_registry.json --dry-run   # read the counts and rejections
npm run flags -- plans/flags/results/registry/FL21_registry.json             # write db-us/flags.json
npm run flags -- --check --strict
npm run flags -- export
npm run flags -- docs
```

## Registry format (`db-us/flags.json`)

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "domains": {
    "D2": { "name": "story / world events", "ranges": [[16, 255]], "persistence": "save", "indexed": true, "lifecycle": "...", "access": "..." }
  },
  "flags": {
    "63": {
      "hex": "$003F", "address": "$0A07", "mask": "$80", "domain": "D2",
      "meanings": [ { "scope": null, "name": "ec_lance_letter_shown", "...": "..." } ]
    }
  },
  "proposals": { "100": [ { "source": "FL21", "name": "...", "summary": "...", "confidence": "medium" } ] }
}
```

- **`domains`**: `ranges` is a list of `[low, high]` global indices (D7 has two). `persistence` is `scene | save | dungeon | none`; `scene` is the only non-persistent value. `indexed: false` (D8 non-bitfield gates, D9 scene-meta gates) has no bit index and takes no records yet (FL40 extends the tool).
- **`flags[index]`**: `domain` is required and must contain the index; `hex`, `address`, `mask` are derived (the tool writes them, fragments must not contain them).
- **`proposals[index]`**: see below. Omitted when empty.

### Meaning fields

| Field | Required | Content |
|-------|----------|---------|
| `scope` | always (the key must be present) | `null` = same meaning everywhere, or `{ "scenes": [ids], "actors": ["file or label"] }`. Scene ids are the decimal ids of `db-us/groups.json`; `actors` is optional and narrows the scope inside a scene |
| `name` | full records | lower snake_case, at least two parts, `<area>_<subject>_<state>`; true when the flag is set; handshakes end in `_req` / `_ack` |
| `area` | full records | a group key of `db-us/groups.json` (`system` for engine flags). Filled in from the scope when all its scenes are in one group |
| `summary` | yes | one sentence: what is true when the flag is set |
| `kinds` | full records | one or more of `once-latch quest-guard quest-done gate-open handshake cutscene-stage puzzle-state reward-claimed form-latch engine idiom unknown` |
| `grade` | full records | `VERIFIED-RUNTIME VERIFIED-STATIC INFERRED UNKNOWN` (`CONTRADICTED` is a verdict recorded against shipped text, not a grade) |
| `stage` | no | `act1.edward_castle` style tag (lowercase, dot-separated) |
| `effects` | no | `{ "set": text, "clear": text }`: what each reader does |
| `requires`, `excludes`, `pairsWith` | no | lists of flag indices or registry names |
| `evidence` | non-`UNKNOWN` grades | `file:line` plus the ROM offset `{n}` of the site (the registry never stores labels) |
| `runtime` | `VERIFIED-RUNTIME` | `{ "result": FR id, "trial": text, "rom": text }` |
| `queue` | advised for `INFERRED`/`UNKNOWN` | runtime-queue ids that would settle it (a warning if missing) |
| `proposedBy` | never written by hand | sources of the proposals the tool consumed when the record was merged |
| `notes` | no | free text (a name guessed from dialog says so here) |
| `level` | no | `full` (default) or `row`: a **row** is the one-line entry for a minor scratch flag (scene, actor, role). It needs only `scope` and `summary` (`name`, `kinds`, `grade` optional) and is allowed for scene-scratch domains only |

### Rules the tool enforces (each one rejects the run)

| Rule | Where |
|------|-------|
| index outside the flag array (0-1439) or outside the domain named on the record | merge, check |
| unknown `kind`, `grade`, `level`, `entry`, `form`, area, scene id | merge, check |
| a D1 (scene scratch) record without a scope | merge, check |
| a persistent flag with a lone scoped meaning ("scope on a global meaning"), or a global meaning next to scoped ones | merge, check |
| two meanings of one index with overlapping scopes, or the same (index, scope) twice in one fragment | merge, check |
| duplicate name: persistent names are unique registry-wide, a scratch name may repeat only at the same index (different scope) and never equals a persistent name | merge, check |
| `VERIFIED-RUNTIME` without `runtime.result`; a grade other than `UNKNOWN` without `evidence` | merge, check |
| editing an existing meaning without `expectOld`, or an `expectOld` that does not match the stored record | merge |
| an unresolved name in `requires` / `excludes` / `pairsWith` | check (a warning at merge time, because the target may arrive in a later fragment) |

Warnings (errors with `--check --strict`): `INFERRED`/`UNKNOWN` without a `queue` id, evidence without `file:line` or `{offset}`, a name prefix that differs from the area prefix, an index in `scene-flags.json` or a preset that is not in the registry yet.

## Fragment format

A fragment has the shape of the registry (the `flags` object restricted to your flags), plus optional `proposals` and `domains`. Top-level keys starting with `_` or `$` are ignored.

```json
{
  "_note": "FL21 fragment",
  "flags": {
    "63": {
      "domain": "D2",
      "meanings": [
        {
          "scope": null,
          "name": "ec_lance_letter_shown",
          "area": "edward_castle",
          "summary": "Will showed Lance's letter to the Edward's Castle left guard.",
          "kinds": ["quest-guard", "once-latch"],
          "grade": "VERIFIED-STATIC",
          "effects": { "set": "The guard lets the player move.", "clear": "The guard sets the joypad lock bits." },
          "evidence": ["extracted/edward_castle/edward_castle/ec0A_left_guard.asm:17"]
        }
      ]
    },
    "2": {
      "domain": "D1",
      "meanings": [
        { "scope": { "scenes": [28] }, "name": "ir_lily_dialog_req", "summary": "...", "kinds": ["handshake"], "grade": "VERIFIED-STATIC", "evidence": ["..."] },
        { "scope": { "scenes": [40] }, "name": "ir_ceiling_trap_b_sprung", "summary": "...", "kinds": ["once-latch"], "grade": "INFERRED", "evidence": ["..."], "queue": ["FL21-03"] }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

A complete, working example is `plans/flags/results/registry/_sample_FL00.json`.

### Editing an existing record

If (index, scope) already has a meaning, an entry for it is rejected unless it carries **`expectOld`**, the guard that proves you edit the record you think you do (same idea as `expectOld` in `merge`):

| `expectOld` | Matches |
|-------------|---------|
| `"ec_old_name"` | the meaning at that index whose `name` equals the text |
| `{ "grade": "inferred", "summary": "letter" }` | every listed field: text fields by case-insensitive substring, other values (arrays, `scope`) by equality (arrays as sets) |

It must match exactly one meaning of the index, otherwise the run is rejected and lists the stored meanings. Three ways to use it, all per entry:

```json
{ "expectOld": "ec_old_name", "scope": null, "name": "ec_new_name", "...": "full replacement meaning" }
{ "expectOld": "ec_lance_letter_shown", "patch": true, "grade": "VERIFIED-RUNTIME", "runtime": { "result": "FR20-01", "trial": "scene $0A with and without flag 63" } }
{ "expectOld": { "name": "ec_obsolete" }, "remove": true }
```

- **Replace** (default): the entry is the whole new meaning (`scope` required). It may change the scope or the name; `proposedBy` is kept.
- **`"patch": true`**: only the listed fields change; `null` removes a field (`"scope": null` means "everywhere"). Use it for grade upgrades from runtime runs.
- **`"remove": true`**: deletes the meaning (and the index when none is left).
- An entry that equals the stored record reports `=unchanged`, so a replace or patch whose result is already stored can be re-applied.

### Proposals (spine flags)

A flag used in several scene groups gets a **proposal** from each group iteration and a record only from the spine iteration:

```json
{ "proposals": { "255": [ { "source": "FL21", "name": "sc_story_beat_done", "summary": "...", "kinds": ["cutscene-stage"], "roles": ["sets in ec0B_prison_door:12", "waits in ec10_kara:30"], "confidence": "low" } ] } }
```

Proposals are stored in `db-us/flags.json` under `proposals[index]`, one per (`source`, scope); re-submitting the same source replaces its proposal. Only an index **without** a record can have proposals. **Promotion**: merging a record for that index consumes all its proposals, removes them and writes their sources into the record's `proposedBy`. The overview below lists the proposals still open.

### Domains

A fragment may carry `"domains": { "D7": { ... } }` to replace a domain definition (for example FL10 refining a range). The result must keep every existing record inside its domain.

## Scene entry spec (`flags -- scene-flags`)

`db-us/scene-flags.json` maps a scene id to what the player needs on arrival. The old three fields keep working; three optional fields were added:

```json
{
  "10": {
    "names": ["ec_lance_letter_shown"],
    "entry": "locked-until-flag",
    "grade": "VERIFIED-RUNTIME",
    "note": "...",
    "source": "..."
  }
}
```

| Field | Content |
|-------|---------|
| `flags` | decimal flag indices: the minimum set that makes the player free on arrival. In a spec it may be omitted when `names` is given (looked up in the registry) |
| `names` | registry names; checked against `db-us/flags.json` when it exists. A name must belong to a persistent flag (scratch flags are cleared at scene load and cannot be an entry requirement), and its index must be in `flags` |
| `entry` | `free` (no flags), `locked-until-flag` (needs flags), `cutscene`, `unreachable`, `unknown` |
| `grade` | same vocabulary as the registry; only runtime-verified entries should ship as `VERIFIED-RUNTIME` |
| `note`, `source` | text |

The spec has the shape of the file (scene id to entry). Editing an existing entry uses `expectOld` (an object `{ field: text or value }`), `patch` and `remove`, as above. `npm run export -- scenes` validates the file against the registry and publishes `requiredFlagNames`, `entry` and `flagGrade` next to `requiredFlags` in `artifacts/scenes.json`.

## Presets spec (`flags -- presets`)

```json
{
  "after_edward_castle": {
    "after": "after_south_cape",
    "flags": [33, 63],
    "flagNames": ["ec_lance_letter_shown"],
    "items": [{ "id": 8, "slot": 0 }],
    "form": "Will",
    "gems": 0,
    "abilities": [],
    "verifyScene": 10,
    "grade": "INFERRED",
    "evidence": ["FL32 milestone M04"]
  }
}
```

The spec is an object keyed by preset name (lower snake_case). `flags` and `grade` are required. **A preset is an absolute snapshot** of the checkpoint (all flags, items, form), not a delta: `after` only orders presets, and `--check` warns when the flags of the preset it follows are not all present. Flags must be persistent; `items` are `{ id: 0-255, slot: 0-15 }` (inventory `$0AB4`-`$0AC3`); `form` is `Will | Freedan | Shadow`; `verifyScene` is the scene FR50 replays it in (a warning when missing). `expectOld`, `patch` and `remove` work as above.

## Export

`npm run flags -- export` first runs the full check (errors abort the export), then writes:

- `artifacts/flags.json`: `flags[]` flat and sorted by index then scope, one row per meaning with `index`, `hex`, `address`, `addressHex`, `mask`, `maskHex`, `domain`, `persistence`, `name`, `level`, `area`, `scope`, `grade`, `summary`, `stage`, `kinds`, `effects`, `requires`, `excludes`, `pairsWith`, `evidence`, `runtime`, `queue`, `proposedBy`, `notes`, and `sites` when an inventory exists; `nameToIndex` (name to global index, unambiguous because a name never maps to two indices); `domains`.
- `artifacts/flag-presets.json`: presets in dependency order with `flags`, `flagBytes` (`flag`, `address`, `mask`) and `byteMasks` (one OR-mask per byte to write), `items`, `form`, `gems`, `abilities`, `verifyScene`, `grade`.

### Inventory contract (FL01)

The sites join reads `plans/flags/inventory.json` (override with `--inventory=`): `{ "sites": [ { "index": <global decimal>, "offset": <decimal ROM offset>, "file": "...", "line": N, "opcode": "...", "role": "...", "scenes": [ids] } ] }`. A site joins a meaning when the index matches and, for a scoped meaning, one of the site's `scenes` is in the scope (a site without `scenes` joins only global meanings). Any other shape is rejected with a message; the old `iog_flag_usage_inventory.json` is not accepted.

`npm run flags -- inventory` (source `src/flag-inventory.ts`) writes that file. It needs the **line-tracked** extraction: run `npm run extract:lt` first (the command stops with that instruction when `extracted/` carries no `; {n}` tags, and when a scanned site has none), and `npm run extract` afterwards if the tags should not stay committed. Site identity is the decimal ROM offset taken from the tag of the instruction line. The output is deterministic (sorted, fixed field order, no timestamps; the SHA-256 of the scanned tree is recorded), so a re-run on the same tree rewrites nothing (`same`); `--dry-run` writes nothing.

Top-level arrays of `inventory.json`:

| Array | Content |
|-------|---------|
| `sites` | Join-ready rows (one global `index` each): `kind` `cop` (the 8 flag COPs `$CC`-`$D3`, byte and word forms; `sense` set/clear for branches), `scene_gate` (`$13 branch < flag, label >` in the `scene_meta` command streams; `scenes` are the scene ids whose record reaches it, `record`, `label`) and `helper_call` (a `flag_helpers.*` call that resolves to exactly one index) |
| `helper_calls` | All calls of `flag_helpers.*` (JSR and JSL): `helper`, `action`, `width`, `resolution` (`constant`, `cop-operand`, `block`, `trace`), `trace` id, `indices` (global) and `wram` (wramFlags-relative, global = relative + `$0400`) as far as resolved |
| `traces` | The bounded dynamic traces (the method text of the old inventory re-derived on the current tree): `method`, `assumptions`, `call_sites`, `candidate_indices`, `candidates` (index, wram index when relevant, evidence rows). Candidates are values bounded by the tables and spawn rows, not proof that each is reached |
| `unresolved_dynamic_helper_inputs` | Helper calls whose index could not be bounded (empty when every call is covered by a trace) |
| `item_sites` | Item COPs `$D4`-`$D7` with `itemId` |
| `switch_sites` | `SwitchCase` whose operand is not `$0000` (`operand`, `region`; the 106 `$0000` sites are only counted) |
| `direct_accesses` | Every direct operand (hex or `!symbol`) in `$0A00`-`$0BFB`; `scope` is `flag_helpers`, `save_code` (`save_system.asm`) or `other` (the ones the inventory is about). `region` (`flags:event`, `flags:wram`, `flags:tail`, `state`), `access` (read/write/rmw), `width`, `flagSymbol` (`$eventFlags` / `$wramFlags` / `$L_wramFlags` references) |
| `unresolved_cop_sites` | Flag COPs whose operand is not a literal (empty today) |
| `files_without_scenes` | Files with sites but no scene (not placed in `scene_actors`, no scene directory key, no scene prefix) |
| `warnings` | Anything the scan could not verify |

`scenes` of a site come from, in order: `scene_actors` placement (`sceneSource` `placement`), the directory scene key of `db-us/groups.json` (`directory`), the file-name prefix such as `ec0A_` (`prefix`), the scene-meta record (`scene_meta`); an empty list with `sceneSource` `none` means unknown. The role is a guess from the opcode only (`set`, `clear`, `branch`, `wait`, `helper call`, `table reference` (reserved: table-driven flags appear as trace candidates, not as sites), `direct read`, plus `direct write` for direct stores): the inventory carries no semantics. `SetDungeonKillFlag` COPs take an enemy number, not a flag index, and are only counted (the enemy numbers are in trace `dungeon_kill_wram_flags`).

## Example: the sample round trip

```
npm run flags -- plans/flags/results/registry/_sample_FL00.json --dry-run
npm run flags -- plans/flags/results/registry/_sample_FL00.json --db-dir=temp/flags-test/db-us
npm run flags -- --check --db-dir=temp/flags-test/db-us
```

# Registry overview (generated)

## Domains

| Dom | Name | Global indices | Bytes | Persistence | Records |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|
| D1 | scene scratch | $0000-$000F | $0A00-$0A01 | scene | 0 |
| D2 | story / world events | $0010-$00FF | $0A02-$0A1F | save | 0 |
| D3 | event triggers / death actions | $0100-$01FF | $0A20-$0A3F | save | 0 |
| D4 | chests, hidden Red Jewels, barriers | $0200-$02FF | $0A40-$0A5F | save | 0 |
| D5 | scene clear reward | $0300-$03FF | $0A60-$0A7F | save | 0 |
| D6 | dungeon kill flags | $0400-$04FF | $0A80-$0A9F | dungeon | 0 |
| D7 | boss reward / ability unlock | $0500-$0507, $0510-$059F | $0AA0-$0AA0, $0AA2-$0AB3 | save | 0 |
| D8 | non-bitfield gates | n/a | n/a | none | 0 |
| D9 | scene-meta gates | n/a | n/a | none | 0 |

## Lifecycle

| Dom | Lifecycle | How it is accessed |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Zeroed by every ClearSceneState (STX $eventFlags with X = 0) and saved, cleared and restored around the inventory overlay; the same index means different things in different scenes (to confirm in FL10 and FR00). | COP $CC-$D3 (byte and word forms), SetFlagRaw/TestFlagRaw, direct LDA $eventFlags. |
| D2 | Part of the save block $0A00-$0BFB; set once by the story and never cleared by the engine. | COP flag opcodes, the *Raw helpers (actor-parameter indices: laborers $A0-$A3, necklace stones $98/$99, statues $F8-$FD, orbs $F2/$F3). |
| D3 | Save block. Flag $0100+n triggers event block n (ApplyAllEventBlocks) or is the death-action index of an enemy. | COP word forms, the *_0100 helpers, event_blocks, enemy death-action indices in scene_actors. |
| D4 | Save block. One flag per chest, hidden jewel or barrier. | The *_0200 helpers (scene_chest_table byte 3, hidden jewel actor parameter, barrier table). |
| D5 | Save block. Flag $0300+scene id marks the reward of a cleared scene as claimed. | The *_0300 helpers (A = scene id). |
| D6 | Global = WRAM-relative wramFlags index + $0400. Zeroed on world-map entry, st68_kara, sp58_red_eye and game over (to confirm in FL10 and FR30). | SetWramFlag, CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag, COP $D8 (index = enemyNum). |
| D7 | Save block. $0500-$0507 are boss reward flags ($0AA0); $0510+ are ability flags that live in abilityBitmask $0AA2 and beyond. | The *_Offset100 helpers (index masked to 3 bits, lands at $0500-$0507), TestFlag_0510 (characterForm*4 + slot). |
| D8 | Items, character form, gems and other bytes of the save block that scripts test; not stored in this registry yet (FL40 extends the tool). | COP $D4-$D7 (items), SwitchCase on $0AD4/$0AA6, direct reads. |
| D9 | A flag index read from a scene-meta command stream; it names a flag of another domain and is documented there (FL10 decodes the table). | $13 <flag> in scene_meta command streams (SceneCmd_Branch). |
